title: A no_std attribute is not proof of no-std compatibility
task: Review a crate advertised as no_std-compatible because lib.rs contains #![no_std].
context: An optional feature explicitly imports std.
A transitive dependency can also enable std through Cargo feature unification.
CI currently builds only the host desktop target.
evidence: No build is run against a target that lacks std.
The crate documentation promises embedded compatibility.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Accept the no_std claim because the crate-level attribute is present.
Add a no-std disabling feature instead of modeling std as an additive capability.
Test only the default desktop feature set.
expected_decision_properties: Distinguish source annotation from actual dependency/target compatibility.
Prefer additive std capability where the feature model permits it.
Require a real no-std target build and meaningful feature combinations in CI.
Inspect transitive dependency features that can reintroduce std or alloc.
unacceptable_reasoning: #![no_std] guarantees all dependencies are also no_std.
Cargo features are isolated per dependency consumer.
Host compilation is sufficient evidence for embedded support.
expected_tradeoffs: broad platform promise vs verification cost
verification_expectations: Build against at least one target that genuinely lacks std.
Inspect dependency feature activation and allocator requirements.
revisit_when: The crate drops its no_std/embedded compatibility promise.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 12: core/alloc/std layers, no_std behavior, additive std features, and cross-compilation.
